title: Capability Blueprint: Inference Service Surface — Chat/Generation/Embed/Rerank, Acceptance Matrix & Go-Live Runway
creator: Maya Singh
description: High-level product requirements and acceptance criteria for a single coherent hosted inference surface covering chat (multi-turn), standard completions/generation, embeddings, and rerank APIs. This document aligns behavioral contracts, rollout gates, testing plan, and a pragmatic go-live checklist to enable a controlled, observable launch across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment lanes.
goals: Define minimal behavioral contract for each surface to guarantee interoperability and predictable client experience
Establish acceptance matrix (QA + SLO + security) that gates go/no-go for launch
Surface rollout plan and fallbacks for degraded capacity or model mismatch
Minimize breaking changes for existing clients while enabling new structured-output features
scope_included: API schemas and canonical examples for chat, completions, embeddings, rerank
Behavioral contracts: deterministic seeding, stop token semantics, function-calling hints
Acceptance metrics: latency, error rate, quality regression thresholds
Automated test harness: unit + integration + perf + eval prompt sets
Operational runbook snippets: regional fallback, model variant rollout, cost-override knobs
scope_excluded: New client SDK releases (handled separately by DX team)
Large model onboarding (model-specific kernels and quantization handled by Model Onboarding WG)
Full enterprise private air-gap packaging (separate Private deployment epic)
Billing contract changes and pricing model redesign
acceptance_criteria: API contract stability: JSON schemas validated against 100% of example payloads in spec tests
Latency SLO: p95 <= 600ms for small-chat requests (<= 128 tokens) in hosted EU/US regions under 70% load
Throughput/backpressure: system returns 429 with documented retry-recommendation when queue depth exceeds configured threshold
Quality regression: new hosted model bundle fails no more than 2% of regression prompts vs baseline for each surface
Embedding similarity: cosine-stability delta <= 0.03 on canonical embedding seed set
Rerank concordance: top-1 accuracy vs golden set >= 92% for prioritized workloads
Security/SLA: SSO and audit logging toggles validated in private sandbox and security review sign-off completed
Operational readiness: alert runbook and dashboard panels present with defined owners and escalation paths
launch_checklist: Finalize API behavioral docs and canonical examples (doc owner: PM)
Merge API contract tests into CI and block merges if schema drift detected
Complete integration tests against runtime staging environment (ENG sign-off)
Run full eval job (1000 prompt set) and verify quality gates; publish evaluation report
Performance soak test: 72-hour run at expected qps for target tier; capture telemetry and compare to baselines
Security review and checklist confirmation (VPC, KMS, audit logs) with Security team
Operator runbook: regional failover steps, model fallback mapping, emergency rollback procedure
Create customer communication template and migration guidance for breaking behavioral changes
Define default quota values and rate-limiting policy for public tier; verify enforcement in staging
Telemetry dashboards live in Console with token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency
Canary rollout plan scheduled: internal canary -> beta customers -> public gradual ramp
Post-launch monitoring window assigned and initial 14-day risk-review meeting scheduled
rollout_plan: Day 0: Internal canary only (redwood-internal orgs) at 5% of traffic for 24 hours
Day 1-3: Invite-only beta with 10 customers; monitor errors, latency, quality signals
Week 1: Gradual ramp to 25% public traffic with automated abort if any critical gate triggers
Week 2-4: Progressive increase to 100% with ongoing quality regression checks every 24h
Fallback rules: automatic model variant swap to verified-compatible model if error rate > 1% or p95 latency exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive 10-minute windows
test_plan: Integration tests across hosted/dedicated/private runtime variants
Quality evals: baseline vs candidate model using curated prompt sets for each surface
Load/perf tests: peak qps and steady-state cost measurements
Chaos tests: simulate KV cache loss, partial kernel failure, and region outage scenarios
Security validation: SSO flows, KMS encryption at rest/in transit, audit log integrity checks
Client compatibility tests: validate older SDKs do not break basic flows (graceful deprecation)
metrics: User-facing: p50/p95 latency per-surface, api error rate, token cost per 1k tokens
Quality: regression rate against golden prompt sets, embedding stability metric
Operational: mean time to detect (MTTD) alerts for route-level failures, mean time to restore (MTTR)
Adoption: number of active orgs using new surface features and top 10 customers' traffic share
risks_mitigations: Risk: Quality regressions from model swaps — Mitigation: block release if eval regression > threshold and enable immediate rollback
Risk: Unexpected cost spike from default batching behavior — Mitigation: set conservative default batching, surface per-route cost, enable budget caps
Risk: Breaking change in stop-token semantics — Mitigation: compatibility mode flag and explicit deprecation schedule
Risk: Regional capacity constraints during ramp — Mitigation: staggered regional rollout and auto-fallback to adjacent region with documented latency trade-offs
